events.title: Thomas Becket Murdered in Canterbury Cathedral
events.description: Four knights loyal to King Henry II of England killed Archbishop Thomas Becket inside Canterbury Cathedral. The attack followed a long and bitter quarrel between the king and his archbishop over the rights of the Church.
events.significance: The murder shocked medieval Europe. Becket was soon declared a saint, and Canterbury became one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Christendom.

events.title: Birth of Andrew Johnson
events.description: Andrew Johnson was born in Raleigh, North Carolina, into poverty. He rose from tailor's apprentice to become the 17th President of the United States.
events.significance: Johnson took office after Abraham Lincoln's assassination and led the country through the early years of Reconstruction. He was the first U.S. president to be impeached.

events.title: Texas Joins the United States
events.description: Texas was admitted to the Union as the 28th state. It had been an independent republic for nearly a decade after breaking away from Mexico.
events.significance: The annexation of Texas increased tensions with Mexico. It helped lead to the Mexican–American War the following year.

events.title: The Wounded Knee Massacre
events.description: U.S. Army soldiers killed hundreds of Lakota men, women and children at Wounded Knee Creek in South Dakota.
events.significance: Wounded Knee is often seen as the tragic end of the Indian Wars on the American Plains. It remains a powerful symbol of the suffering of Native Americans.
